source_review.notes: Checked the current DLA ASSIST record for MIL-STD-882E Change 1; both NASA System Safety Handbook volumes and NASA's system-safety guidance index; the active NASA-STD-8739.8B record and standard; current OSHA 29 CFR 1910.119 and Appendix C; current NIOSH control hierarchy; and the FAA SMS policy index. All ten final URLs returned HTTP 200. Normative requirements, agency guidance, occupational examples, and chapter synthesis are distinguished.

evidence: Reviewed the hazard-to-scenario-to-control-to-requirement-to-verification-to-acceptance evidence chain.
Reviewed the policy lookup expression R=M(S,L) and rejection of unsupported category multiplication.
Reviewed the scenario tuple separating initiation, contributors, exposure, hazardous state, controls, and consequence.
Reviewed bounded residual-risk acceptance notation for risk, configuration, and operating scope.
notation_and_syntax.notes: All symbols are locally defined and categorical risk labels are explicitly ordinal rather than interval or ratio measurements.

evidence: Executed system-safety-hazard-register-fixture under python3 with exact output recorded in artifacts/snippets/SYSENG-066/report.json.
Confirmed five unique and complete synthetic rows and five verified controls.
Confirmed four controls occupy the first three declared precedence levels and one is a warning-level control.
Recomputed four initially high-or-serious categories and two residually high-or-serious categories through explicit lookup.
Confirmed five named acceptance-authority fields and one open action.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The computation checks declared metadata consistency only; it does not validate risk categories, control effectiveness, acceptance authority, or real-system safety.

evidence: Confirmed ordered severity and likelihood categories do not justify multiplication, averaging, or cardinal distance claims.
Confirmed the approved matrix is modeled as a lookup function rather than a product.
Confirmed scenario and traceability relations preserve many-to-many causality and control allocation.
Confirmed residual-risk acceptance is bounded by configuration and scope instead of acting as a permanent global predicate.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The chapter presents a decision model, not a probabilistic theorem or a universal quantitative safety equation.

evidence: Challenged nominal, degraded, emergency, maintenance, transport, storage, modification, recovery, retirement, and disposal modes.
Reviewed physical energy/material, software timing/state/data, human workload, organizational context, cyber-induced unsafe state, and external-service hazards.
Reviewed common power, sensor, code, requirements, environment, location, maintenance, calibration, supplier, and authority dependencies.
Reviewed severity-versus-likelihood confusion, exposure double counting, matrix boundary effects, uncertainty, and improbable-not-impossible cases.
Reviewed bypass, temporary restrictions, waivers, transferred and introduced hazards, aggregate risk, field anomalies, and configuration change.
Reviewed all ten worked examples and five complete answers for assumptions, intermediate reasoning, evidence limits, and bounded conclusions.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Production use requires domain regulator/certification, safety, operator/maintainer, human-factors, software, cybersecurity, reliability, configuration, emergency-response, environmental, legal, technical-authority, and risk-acceptance review.

evidence: Confirmed causes, hazards, hazardous events, exposure, mishaps, and consequences remain distinct.
Confirmed initial risk is preserved and current/residual risk credits only implemented evidence-backed controls.
Confirmed control precedence prioritizes elimination and design over warnings and administrative action.
Confirmed each credited control requires traceability through requirement, allocation, implementation, verification result, and configuration.
Confirmed acceptance names authorized role and bounded configuration, period, restrictions, and reopen criteria.
Confirmed no individual analysis technique or incident-free period is presented as proof of completeness or safety.
invariant_checking.notes: A colored register cell, issued document, or passed component test never substitutes for the end-to-end evidence and decision chain.

proof_review.notes: The chapter provides reasoning structures and invariant checks but no theorem proof.

proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No passage is presented as a proof sketch.

evidence: The executable result is labeled synthetic_metadata_only.
The fixture explicitly denies completeness, category calibration, control adequacy, independence, and real-system safety claims.
Standards and agency guidance are attributed without claiming compliance or certification.
Incident-free operation and analogous evidence are bounded by exposure, reporting, configuration, and transfer limitations.
No external review, accepted production risk, verified operational control, or system-safety approval is claimed.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Observed local code execution, source-backed guidance, and production assurance claims remain explicitly separated.

conceptual_review.notes: Internal conceptual review checked hazard, mishap, scenario, severity, likelihood, risk, initial/current/residual risk, control, safety constraint, hazard log, acceptance, ordinal matrices, exposure, lifecycle scope, and defeasible closure.

practitioner_review.notes: Internal practitioner-oriented review checked governance, retrieval, hazard statements, complementary methods, control precedence, requirement derivation, integrated verification/validation, software, cyber, human context, hazard-log fields, change, operational feedback, emergency response, aggregate risk, and retirement.

pedagogical_review.notes: Internal pedagogical review confirmed progression from definitions and governance through scenario construction, risk judgment, control design, evidence, acceptance, and lifecycle feedback. Ten distinct examples and five complete solutions exercise analysis, critique, verification, socio-technical interaction, and change decisions.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external DoD/NASA/OSHA/FAA/NIOSH standards expert, regulator/certification authority, domain safety engineer, operator/maintainer, human-factors specialist, software/data/cybersecurity owner, reliability analyst, environmental/emergency-response authority, legal authority, independent V&V reviewer, technical authority, or residual-risk acceptance authority review is claimed.
